subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: A public issue shall be kept open for-

options.A: at least 3 days and not more than 10 days
options.B: at least 3 days and not more than 7 days
options.C: at least 5 days and not more than 15 days
options.D: at least 7 days and not more than 21 days

answer_html:
Answer: (A) at least 3 days and not more than 10 days.

An issue must remain open for a minimum of 3 days and cannot be kept open for more than 10 days. The other eligibility conditions in the same set include an application to one or more stock exchanges for in-principle approval, an agreement with a depository for dematerialisation, and all existing partly paid-up equity shares being either fully paid up or forfeited.
topic_text: Period for which an issue is kept open

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The minimum subscription which must be received in a public issue is-

options.A: 100% of the issue size, no part of which may be waived by the lead merchant banker to the issue
options.B: 90% of the issue size, failing which the application money must be refunded within 15 days of closure
options.C: 75% of the issue size, failing which the application money must be refunded within 30 days of closure
options.D: 50% of the issue size, failing which the issue is deemed to have been withdrawn by the issuer company

answer_html:
Answer: (B) 90% of the issue size, failing which the application money must be refunded within 15 days of closure.

The minimum subscription is 90% of the issue size. If it is not received the application money has to be refunded within 15 days of the closure of the issue. This is distinct from the requirement that firm arrangements of finance through verifiable means have been made towards 75% of the stated means of finance, excluding the amount to be raised through the proposed issue and existing identifiable internal accruals.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under the profitability route to an initial public offer the issuer must have a minimum average pre-tax operating profit, calculated on a restated and consolidated basis, of-

options.A: ₹15 crore during each of the 3 financial years immediately preceding the year of the issue
options.B: ₹3 crore during the 3 most profitable years out of the immediately preceding 5 financial years
options.C: ₹25 crore during the 5 financial years immediately preceding the year of the issue, taken together
options.D: ₹15 crore during the 3 most profitable years out of the immediately preceding 5 years

answer_html:
Answer: (D) ₹15 crore during the 3 most profitable years out of the immediately preceding 5 years.

The requirement is a minimum average pre-tax operating profit of ₹15 crore, restated and consolidated, during the 3 most profitable years out of the immediately preceding 5 years. It sits alongside the requirement of net tangible assets of at least ₹3 crore in each of the preceding 3 years and a net worth of at least ₹1 crore in each of the preceding 3 full years.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The condition that not more than 50% of the net tangible assets may be held in monetary assets does not apply at all where-

options.A: the issue size does not exceed ₹100 crore, so that no monitoring agency has to be appointed
options.B: the initial public offer is made entirely through an offer for sale by the existing shareholders
options.C: the issuer is a Government company in which the whole of the capital is held by the Government
options.D: the issue is made through the book building process rather than through a fixed price issue

answer_html:
Answer: (B) the initial public offer is made entirely through an offer for sale by the existing shareholders.

The issuer must have net tangible assets of at least ₹3 crore in each of the preceding 3 years of 12 months each, of which not more than 50% are held in monetary assets. Where more than 50% is so held the issuer has to make a firm commitment to utilise the excess in its business or project. The 50% criterion does not apply where the initial public offer is made entirely through an offer for sale.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: An issuer which does not satisfy any of the stipulated eligibility conditions may still make an initial public offer if-

options.A: the issue is made through the book building process and the issuer undertakes to allot at least 50% of the net offer to public to qualified institutional buyers, whatever the level of subscription received
options.B: the issue is underwritten in full by a merchant banker registered with the Board and the promoters of the issuer undertake to subscribe to any shortfall in the minimum subscription received
options.C: the issuer obtains a grading for its initial public offer from at least two credit rating agencies registered with the Board and discloses that grading prominently in the offer document
options.D: the issue is made through the book building process and the issuer undertakes to allot at least 75% of the net offer to public to qualified institutional buyers, refunding the subscription money if it fails

answer_html:
Answer: (D) the issue is made through the book building process and the issuer undertakes to allot at least 75% of the net offer to public to qualified institutional buyers, refunding the subscription money if it fails.

Any issuer not satisfying the eligibility conditions may make an initial public offer if the issue is made through the book building process and the issuer undertakes to allot at least 75% of the net offer to public to qualified institutional buyers and to refund the full subscription monies if it fails to do so. Obtaining an IPO grading from a credit rating agency is permitted but is not a substitute for the conditions.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: In an issue made through the book building process under the ordinary route, the allocation in the net offer to public category is-

options.A: not less than 50% to retail individual investors, not less than 15% to non-institutional investors and not more than 35% to qualified institutional buyers
options.B: a minimum of 30% to retail individual investors, the remainder going to other individual applicants and to corporate bodies without any further sub-limit
options.C: not less than 35% to retail individual investors, not less than 15% to non-institutional investors and not more than 50% to qualified institutional buyers
options.D: not more than 10% to retail individual investors, not more than 15% to non-institutional investors and not less than 75% to qualified institutional buyers

answer_html:
Answer: (C) not less than 35% to retail individual investors, not less than 15% to non-institutional investors and not more than 50% to qualified institutional buyers.

The ordinary book building allocation is not less than 35% to retail individual investors, not less than 15% to non-institutional investors and not more than 50% to qualified institutional buyers, 5% of the qualified institutional buyer portion being allocated to mutual funds. The 10 / 15 / 75 split applies to an issue made under sub-regulation (2) of regulation 6, and the 30% floor for retail investors applies where the issue is made otherwise than through book building.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: In an initial public offer the minimum promoters contribution and the lock-in applicable to it are-

options.A: 20% of the post issue capital, locked in for 3 years from the date of commencement of commercial production or the date of allotment, whichever is later
options.B: 20% of the pre issue capital, locked in for 1 year from the date of allotment in the public issue, whatever the date of commencement of commercial production
options.C: 25% of the post issue capital, locked in for 3 years from the date of allotment in the public issue, whatever the date of commencement of production
options.D: 20% of the post issue capital, locked in for 1 year, the holding in excess of that contribution being locked in for the longer period of 3 years

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 20% of the post issue capital, locked in for 3 years from the date of commencement of commercial production or the date of allotment, whichever is later.

The minimum promoters contribution should not be less than 20% of the post issue capital and is locked in for 3 years from the date of commencement of commercial production or the date of allotment in the public issue, whichever is later. Promoters holding in excess of the minimum contribution is locked in for 1 year, and excess promoters contribution in a further public offer is not subject to lock-in at all.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The face value of an equity share offered in a public issue-

options.A: shall in every case be ₹10 per share, the issuer being free to fix any premium it wishes above that face value
options.B: may be fixed at any amount the issuer chooses, the only condition being that the issue price is not below it
options.C: may be below ₹10 but not below ₹1 where the issue price is ₹500 or more per share, and shall otherwise be ₹10 per share
options.D: may be below ₹10 but not below ₹1 where the issue price is ₹100 or more per share, and shall otherwise be ₹5 per share

answer_html:
Answer: (C) may be below ₹10 but not below ₹1 where the issue price is ₹500 or more per share, and shall otherwise be ₹10 per share.

The face value may be less than ₹10 but not less than ₹1 if the issue price is ₹500 or more per share. If the issue price is less than ₹500 the face value shall be ₹10 per share. Separately, the issue price itself shall not be less than the face value.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: An issuer proposes to offer equity shares to retail individual investors at a price below the price at which the net offer is made to the other categories of applicants. It may do so provided the price offered to the retail investors is-

options.A: not lower than the price to the other categories by more than 10%
options.B: not lower than the price to the other categories by more than 5%
options.C: not lower than the price offered to the anchor investors in the issue
options.D: not lower than the floor price stated in the red herring prospectus

answer_html:
Answer: (A) not lower than the price to the other categories by more than 10%.

Retail individual investors, shareholders entitled to reservation and employees may be offered equity shares at a price which is not lower than the price at which the net offer is made to the other categories by more than 10%. In a book built issue the price to an anchor investor cannot be lower than the price offered to other applicants, and under the alternate method of book building the difference between the floor price and the price to employees cannot exceed 10% of the floor price.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Which of the following is NOT ordinarily included in unpublished price sensitive information?

options.A: A change in the key managerial personnel of the company whose securities are listed
options.B: The appointment of a new registrar and share transfer agent by the company
options.C: A change in the capital structure of the company whose securities are listed
options.D: The declaration of a dividend by the company whose securities are listed

answer_html:
Answer: (B) The appointment of a new registrar and share transfer agent by the company.

Unpublished price sensitive information means information relating to a company or its securities which is not generally available and which, on becoming generally available, is likely to materially affect the price of the securities. It ordinarily includes financial results, dividends, change in capital structure, mergers, de-mergers, acquisitions, delistings, disposals and expansion of business, and changes in key managerial personnel.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under the Prohibition of Insider Trading Regulations, 2015, an insider is-

options.A: only a director, officer or employee of the listed company whose securities are being traded in the market
options.B: only a person who has actually dealt in the securities of the company concerned while holding office in it
options.C: any person holding more than ten per cent of the voting rights in the listed company whose shares are traded
options.D: a connected person, or a person in possession of or having access to unpublished price sensitive information

answer_html:
Answer: (D) a connected person, or a person in possession of or having access to unpublished price sensitive information.

An insider is any person who is a connected person, or who is in possession of or has access to unpublished price sensitive information. Actual dealing is not part of the definition; a person becomes an insider by reason of the connection or the possession of the information, and the prohibition on trading then applies to him.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: A connected person is one who is, or has during a stated period prior to the concerned act been, associated with a company in a capacity which allows access to unpublished price sensitive information. That period is-

options.A: three months
options.B: twelve months
options.C: twenty-four months
options.D: six months

answer_html:
Answer: (D) six months.

The association must be during the six months prior to the concerned act. The connection may arise by reason of frequent communication with the officers of the company, or of a contractual, fiduciary or employment relationship, or of being a director, officer or employee, or of a professional or business relationship whether temporary or permanent. Certain persons, such as an immediate relative, a holding or subsidiary company, an intermediary, or a banker of the company, are deemed connected unless the contrary is established.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: An insider is required to make a continual disclosure of a trade-

options.A: within 30 days, where the value traded over any financial year aggregates in excess of ₹25 lakh
options.B: within 2 trading days, where the value traded over any calendar quarter aggregates in excess of ₹10 lakh
options.C: within 2 trading days, where the value traded over any calendar month aggregates in excess of ₹10 lakh
options.D: within 7 trading days, where the value traded over any calendar quarter aggregates in excess of ₹5 lakh

answer_html:
Answer: (B) within 2 trading days, where the value traded over any calendar quarter aggregates in excess of ₹10 lakh.

Continual disclosures are to be made within two trading days of the transaction where the value of the securities traded, over any calendar quarter, aggregates to a traded value in excess of ₹10 lakh. That is separate from the initial disclosure, which requires a key managerial personnel or a director to disclose his holding of securities of the company as on the date of his appointment.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: A trading plan formulated by an insider and approved by the compliance officer-

options.A: may be departed from by the insider where market conditions change materially after the plan is disclosed
options.B: need not be notified to the stock exchanges, approval by the compliance officer being sufficient by itself
options.C: shall not entail commencement of trading earlier than six months from the public disclosure of the plan
options.D: shall not entail commencement of trading earlier than three months from the approval by the compliance officer

answer_html:
Answer: (C) shall not entail commencement of trading earlier than six months from the public disclosure of the plan.

An insider formulates a trading plan and presents it to the compliance officer for approval and public disclosure. The plan cannot entail commencement of trading on behalf of the insider earlier than six months from the public disclosure of the plan, and it cannot be deviated from. On approval the compliance officer notifies the plan to the stock exchanges on which the securities are listed.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The structured digital database containing the nature of the unpublished price sensitive information must be preserved for a period of not less than-

options.A: three years
options.B: ten years
options.C: eight years
options.D: five years

answer_html:
Answer: (C) eight years.

The organisation must maintain internally a structured digital database containing the nature of the unpublished price sensitive information, with adequate internal controls, and must preserve it for a period of not less than eight years, and for longer where an investigation is on foot.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: In a proceeding concerning trading while in possession of unpublished price sensitive information, the onus of proof is placed as follows-

options.A: the person charged must establish his innocence in every case, the regulations admitting of no defence to the charge
options.B: a connected person must show he was not in possession of the information; otherwise the onus lies on the Board
options.C: the Board must establish that the person was in possession of the information, whether or not he is a connected person
options.D: a connected person must establish that he did not trade at all, while in other cases the Board must establish that he did

answer_html:
Answer: (B) a connected person must show he was not in possession of the information; otherwise the onus lies on the Board.

No insider shall trade in securities listed or proposed to be listed when in possession of unpublished price sensitive information, though the insider may prove his innocence by the defences available. In the case of connected persons the onus of establishing that they were not in possession of the information rests on those persons, and in other cases the onus is on the Board.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under the minimum standards for the code of conduct, the trading window may be re-opened, and a pre-cleared trade must be executed, respectively-

options.A: not earlier than two trading days after the information becomes generally available, and within not more than ten days
options.B: immediately upon the information becoming generally available, and within not more than fifteen trading days thereafter
options.C: not earlier than 48 hours after the information becomes generally available, and within not more than seven trading days
options.D: not earlier than 24 hours after the information becomes generally available, and within not more than two trading days

answer_html:
Answer: (C) not earlier than 48 hours after the information becomes generally available, and within not more than seven trading days.

The timing for re-opening the trading window is determined by the compliance officer, taking into account the unpublished price sensitive information becoming generally available and capable of assimilation by the market, and in any event shall not be earlier than forty-eight hours after the information becomes generally available. The code of conduct must also specify a reasonable time frame, not more than seven trading days, within which a pre-cleared trade has to be executed, failing which fresh pre-clearance is needed.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: A takeover in which the promoters of the target company voluntarily sell their shares to the acquirer at an attractive price offered by him is called a-

options.A: friendly takeover
options.B: hostile takeover
options.C: vertical takeover
options.D: conglomerate takeover

answer_html:
Answer: (A) friendly takeover.

In a friendly takeover the promoters of the target company voluntarily sell their shares at an attractive price offered by the acquirer. In a hostile takeover they resist and fight back to defend their ownership or control. A horizontal takeover is of a company in the same industry, a vertical takeover is of a supplier or a customer, and a conglomerate takeover is of a company operating in a wholly different industry.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Shares of a target company are frequently traded shares where the traded turnover on any stock exchange during the twelve calendar months preceding the calendar month in which the public announcement is made is at least-

options.A: 10% of the total number of shares of that class of the target company
options.B: 25% of the total number of shares of that class of the target company
options.C: 5% of the total number of shares of that class of the target company
options.D: 50% of the total number of shares of that class of the target company

answer_html:
Answer: (A) 10% of the total number of shares of that class of the target company.

Frequently traded shares are shares of a target company in which the traded turnover on any stock exchange during the twelve calendar months preceding the calendar month in which the public announcement is made is at least 10% of the total number of shares of such class of the target company. Whether shares are frequently traded matters because deposit of such shares, if also freely transferable, is one of the permitted forms of the escrow.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Continual disclosure of shareholding as on 31 March, within seven working days from the end of the financial year, has to be made by-

options.A: the promoters alone, a non-promoter being under no obligation whatever the size of the shareholding held
options.B: the promoters irrespective of their shareholding, and non-promoters holding along with their PACs more than 25%
options.C: every shareholder holding more than 5% of the shares of the target company, whether he is a promoter or not
options.D: the target company itself, no obligation of disclosure being cast on the acquirer under these regulations

answer_html:
Answer: (B) the promoters irrespective of their shareholding, and non-promoters holding along with their PACs more than 25%.

The disclosure of shareholding as on 31 March is to be made within 7 working days from the end of each financial year, to every stock exchange where the shares of the target company are listed and to the registered office of the target company. It is made by the promoters irrespective of their shareholding and by non-promoters holding along with persons acting in concert more than 25% of the shares. There is no obligation on the target company itself to make event based disclosure; the obligation is on the acquirer, the promoter and their persons acting in concert.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: An open offer which has been made may be withdrawn where-

options.A: the statutory approvals required for the offer have been refused, or the acquirer being a natural person has died
options.B: the acquirer finds that the market price of the shares of the target company has risen since the announcement
options.C: the acquirer has been unable to arrange the finances required for the payment of the offer consideration
options.D: the board of directors of the target company recommends to the shareholders that they should not tender

answer_html:
Answer: (A) the statutory approvals required for the offer have been refused, or the acquirer being a natural person has died.

Withdrawal is permitted where the statutory approvals required have been refused, where the acquirer being a natural person has died, where a condition stipulated in the agreement for acquisition is not met, and in any circumstances which in the opinion of SEBI merit withdrawal. Within 2 working days the merchant banker must announce the withdrawal in the newspapers with the reasons and grounds, and simultaneously inform SEBI, the stock exchanges and the registered office of the target company.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
case_facts_html:
Palghat Ceramics Limited, whose equity shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange, has a total voting share capital of 10 crore equity shares of ₹10 each, fully paid up.

Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited, together with the persons acting in concert with it, holds 1.8 crore shares in Palghat Ceramics Limited. On 5 June 2025 it enters into an agreement with an existing shareholder to acquire a further 1.2 crore shares of the target company.

The promoters of Palghat Ceramics Limited, who are unconnected with Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited, hold 4 crore shares, and the balance of the share capital is held by the public.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. On completion of the agreed acquisition, the position is that the acquisition-

options.A: attracts the obligation to make a public announcement of an open offer, the post acquisition holding reaching 30% of the voting rights
options.B: does not attract that obligation, because the shares are being acquired from an existing shareholder and not from the public at large
options.C: does not attract that obligation, because the acquirer will still hold less than the 40% of the voting rights held by the promoters
options.D: attracts that obligation only if the acquirer simultaneously acquires control over the management of the target company

answer_html:
Answer: (A) attracts the obligation to make a public announcement of an open offer, the post acquisition holding reaching 30% of the voting rights.

The acquirer holds 1.8 crore of the 10 crore shares, that is 18% of the voting rights, and the agreement takes its holding to 3 crore shares or 30%. Where the post acquisition holding of an acquirer along with its persons acting in concert reaches or exceeds 25% of the voting rights the initial trigger is touched, and an obligation is cast on the acquirer to make a public announcement of an open offer. It is immaterial that the shares come from an existing shareholder rather than from the market, and control is not a separate condition.
source_file: CMA FINAL Paper 13 corporate laws Dec26.pdf

Palghat Ceramics Limited, whose equity shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange, has a total voting share capital of 10 crore equity shares of ₹10 each, fully paid up.

Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited, together with the persons acting in concert with it, holds 1.8 crore shares in Palghat Ceramics Limited. On 5 June 2025 it enters into an agreement with an existing shareholder to acquire a further 1.2 crore shares of the target company.

The promoters of Palghat Ceramics Limited, who are unconnected with Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited, hold 4 crore shares, and the balance of the share capital is held by the public.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. The open offer which Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited must make has to be for the acquisition of at least-

options.A: 2.50 crore shares
options.B: 1.20 crore shares
options.C: 5.60 crore shares
options.D: 2.60 crore shares

answer_html:
Answer: (D) 2.60 crore shares.

On touching the initial trigger the acquirer must make a public announcement of an open offer for the acquisition of an additional 26% of the shares of the target company. That is 26% of 10 crore shares, or 2.60 crore shares. Applying the 25% trigger percentage instead gives 2.50 crore shares, taking the triggering acquisition itself gives 1.20 crore shares, and adding the 26% to the 30% already held gives 5.60 crore shares.

Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited, together with the persons acting in concert with it, holds 1.8 crore shares in Palghat Ceramics Limited. On 5 June 2025 it enters into an agreement with an existing shareholder to acquire a further 1.2 crore shares of the target company.

The promoters of Palghat Ceramics Limited, who are unconnected with Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited, hold 4 crore shares, and the balance of the share capital is held by the public.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. In the financial year 2026-27 Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited, then holding 3 crore shares, acquires a further 45 lakh shares from the market and now proposes to acquire another 10 lakh shares in that same financial year. The position is-

options.A: the further acquisition is permitted without any open offer, because the acquirer already holds more than 25% of the voting rights
options.B: the further acquisition is prohibited outright, an acquirer holding 25% or more being barred from making any creeping acquisition
options.C: the further acquisition needs a prior open offer for an additional 26%, the aggregate acquisition in the financial year exceeding 5%
options.D: the further acquisition is permitted without any open offer, because each of the two acquisitions taken by itself is below the 5% ceiling

answer_html:
Answer: (C) the further acquisition needs a prior open offer for an additional 26%, the aggregate acquisition in the financial year exceeding 5%.

An acquirer who has already acquired 25% or more of the shares shall not acquire more than 5% of the shares of the target company within any financial year, which begins on 1 April, without a prior public announcement of an open offer for an additional 26%. The ceiling applies to the aggregate acquired in the year, not to each acquisition separately: 45 lakh shares is 4.5% and the proposed 10 lakh shares is a further 1%, taking the aggregate to 5.5%. Any acquisition must in any event leave the minimum public shareholding of 25% intact.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
case_facts_html:
Palghat Ceramics Limited, whose equity shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange, has a total voting share capital of 10 crore equity shares of ₹10 each, fully paid up.

Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited, together with the persons acting in concert with it, holds 1.8 crore shares in Palghat Ceramics Limited. On 5 June 2025 it enters into an agreement with an existing shareholder to acquire a further 1.2 crore shares of the target company.

The promoters of Palghat Ceramics Limited, who are unconnected with Ratnagiri Holdings Private Limited, hold 4 crore shares, and the balance of the share capital is held by the public.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. During the offer period the Board of Palghat Ceramics Limited proposes to fix a record date for a bonus issue on the second working day before the tendering period commences, and to sell a material undertaking outside the ordinary course of business. The position is that-

options.A: both courses are open to it, the obligation of the target company during the offer period being confined to conducting its business in the ordinary course consistent with its past practice
options.B: the record date may be fixed but the undertaking may not be sold, the bar on fixing a record date operating only from the first working day before the tendering period commences
options.C: the undertaking may be sold but the record date may not be fixed, the alienation of material assets being within the ordinary powers of the board throughout the offer period
options.D: neither course is open to it: no record date may be fixed from the third working day before the tendering period, and material assets need a special resolution by postal ballot

answer_html:
Answer: (D) neither course is open to it: no record date may be fixed from the third working day before the tendering period, and material assets need a special resolution by postal ballot.

The target company is prohibited from fixing any record date for a corporate action on or after the third working day prior to the commencement of the tendering period and until the expiry of that period, so a record date on the second working day before it is not permissible. During the offer period the board of the target company or of any of its subsidiaries may not alienate any material assets by sale, lease, encumbrance or otherwise outside the ordinary course of business unless the shareholders approve by a special resolution passed by postal ballot.
